method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs
why_not_one_block_off: The corridor is lettered in the roadway on both sheets: sheet 76 prints 'AVE. H OR BALL' vertically in it on view 2 (native ~2170) and again on view 3, and sheet 84 prints the identical 'AVE. H OR BALL' on view 1 (native ~1167) and again on view 2. The printed hundred-block runs confirm it independently on each sheet, because the address series restarts at every lettered avenue (F=600, G=700, H=800, I=900, J=1000). Sheet 76: the block west of the chosen corridor carries 701-723 odd / 702-724 even along 38th and 39th Sts (700 block) and the block east of it carries 801-823 / 802-824 (800 block); the next corridor west is lettered 'AVE. G OR WINNIE' (native ~1168, breaking 600 from 700) and the next east is 'AVE. I OR SEALY' (native ~3160, breaking 800 from 900). Sheet 84: the same break - 701-723 / 702-724 west of the chosen corridor, 801-823 / 802-824 east of it; the next corridor west is 'AVE. G OR WINNIE' (native ~162, breaking 600 from 700) and the next east is 'AVE. I OR SEALY' (native ~2170), beyond which the 900 block runs 901-923 / 902-924 up to 'AVE. J OR BROADWAY' (native ~3160, view 3). So the avenue one block west (Ave G) is excluded because on both sheets it is the line that starts the 700 block, not the 800 block, and the avenue one block east (Ave I) is excluded because on both sheets it starts the 900 block. This pair is the near-equal-native-x trap in its sharpest form and it was explicitly not used: sheet 76's Ave G (native 1168.0) sits within 3 px of sheet 84's Ave H (native 1165.1), so matching on similar native x would have tied Ave G to Ave H and sheared the row by a full block. The two sheets' plates are offset by almost exactly one avenue: sheet 76 shows F-G-H-I at ~164 / 1168 / 2171 / ~3160 while sheet 84 shows G-H-I-J at ~162 / 1165 / ~2170 / ~3160. Only the lettering and the hundred-block runs decide it. The red position marker was ignored; on sheet 76 view 2 it lies inside a block on lot lines, and the 20 ft dashed mid-block alleys carrying 6" W. PIPE measure ~60 native px against ~211 native px for the avenue roadway, and no address hundred changes across them (701-711 continue 713-723).
notes: Native x is the roadway CENTRELINE, the midpoint of the two long street-casing lines read against the green native-pixel ruler. Sheet 76 Ave H casings: 2065.6/2277.1 (view 2) and 2065.4/2277.3 (view 3) -> centre 2171.4 on both, roadway width 211.5-211.9 native px = 69.8-70.0 ft at 3.03 px/ft, matching the printed 70' label. Sheet 84 Ave H casings: 1061.8/1268.9 (view 1) and 1061.2/1268.3 (view 2) -> centre 1165.4 / 1164.8, width 207.1 native px = 68.4 ft. Consistency check on the identification: the sheet-76-minus-sheet-84 offset measured independently on Ave H is +1006.3 px and on Ave G is +1005.9 px, agreeing to 0.4 px; a one-avenue misidentification would have shifted one of these by ~1004 px.
